sections.skill: Tell interface and account limits from model abilities

questions.prompt: A free plan stops you after 20 messages a day. Is this a model limit or an account limit?

choices.text: A model limit, because the model itself gets tired and cannot answer more than twenty messages
A law that limits all users

questions.correct_answer: An account limit
questions.intro: Some limits come from your ACCOUNT or INTERFACE, not from what a model can do. A free plan may limit how many messages you send, how long answers can be, or which features you see; a school or work network may block a site; an app may lack a feature that the same company's website has. So "the AI can't do X" sometimes means "this product, plan or network doesn't allow X here." Before deciding a task is impossible, check the plan, settings and help pages. Also know how to get SUPPORT and how to CANCEL a paid plan, including renewal dates.

sections.skill: Compare plan limits with a gym membership

questions.prompt: Why can a basic member not use the pool?

choices.text: The membership does not include it
Because the pool cannot hold water and is permanently closed for every member

questions.correct_answer: The membership does not include it
questions.intro: A gym with a BASIC membership might let you use the treadmills but not the pool. That does not mean the pool cannot hold water; your membership does not include it. The gym's website might also let you book classes that its app cannot. AI products work the same way: what you can do depends on the plan and the app, not only on what the model behind it can do.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: A free trial turned into a paid plan without Jo noticing. What habit would have prevented this?

choices.text: Noting the renewal date and how to cancel
Using the trial as much as possible every day

questions.correct_answer: Noting the renewal date and how to cancel
questions.intro: Account details cause real surprises: a free trial that turns into a paid plan unless canceled, a renewal date that passes unnoticed, a family member using the same login, or a school account that loses access when a student graduates. Keep a note of what you signed up for, the price, the renewal date and how to cancel. If a feature disappears, check the provider's help pages or status page before assuming your work is lost. Save important work outside the tool.
